title: The service manager rings back: eighty dollars off, and whose mistake it was
purpose: Story S8, the call back. Greg lets the customer say it again, owns both mistakes, takes off the difference and a little more, and gives the new total to the cent. It is outbound, so it is not judged; it is the call that keeps call 10's promise.

call.day: slot 4's next working day after call 10 (rule R6; card S08, call 11)

scenario.who_calls: Greg Whitaker rings Frank Daugherty, as Travis promised, fifty minutes before the time Travis gave.
scenario.job: timing belt, tensioner, idlers and water pump, done
scenario.what_happens: Greg says he has read the write-up and listened to the quote call, asks to hear it from the customer, owns the price and the day, takes 80 dollars off and says what that makes the bill; the customer accepts and will collect the car that afternoon.

facts.note: 741.60 - 688.00 = 53.60. 741.60 - 80.00 = 661.60 before tax, 722.80 with sales tax. 80 on 741.60 is 10.8 %, above the 10 % rule, and the approval is his own (card S08, question S8.2).

script.said: Hello.
Mr. Daugherty? Greg Whitaker, Brennan Auto Care.
Yeah. Travis said you'd call.
Yes sir. I've read what Travis wrote up, and I've listened to the call where you got your price. I'd like to hear it from you, though, if you've got a minute.
It's simple. Y'all told me six eighty-eight, same day. It took two days and the bill was eight-ten. I planned around that car. I had to borrow my son-in-law's truck to get to Knoxville.
Yes sir.
That's what I've got too. You were quoted six eighty-eight, and you were promised Monday. Neither one was right, and both of those are on us. I'll own that.
Well. I appreciate you sayin' it.

Here's what I can do. The right price for the job is seven-twenty, and with shop supplies your bill was seven forty-one sixty before tax. The difference from what you were told is fifty-three sixty. I'm taking eighty dollars off — the difference, and the rest for the day you were without it.
Alright.
So what's that come to?
Six sixty-one sixty before tax. Seven twenty-two eighty out the door.
Seven twenty-two.
And eighty cents. That's less than the six eighty-eight would've come to with tax.
...Alright. That's fair. I'll come get it this afternoon.
It's ready now, and it's been road-tested. We're here till five-thirty. Ask for me or for Travis, either one.
Okay.
And the boy that quoted me?
Caleb's new, and he's a good one. He read you a number off a page I should've had fixed. That's getting corrected.
Alright, Greg. I'll see you this afternoon.
Thank you, Mr. Daugherty. I'll have the paperwork ready.

truth.note: Not judged: an outbound call carries no verdict (judged: false). What happened: the discount was given and accepted.
truth.outcome: 80.00 off, approved by slot 4; the customer collects the car and pays 722.80 that afternoon

why.verdict: None. The product does not judge outbound calls. In the call log this is the call that makes call 10's promise 'kept'.

day_report.why: Not a judged call, and slot 4 has no desk on the public line. It shows in Travis's report as the call back that was kept (call 10).

new_facts: Slot 4 listened to the recording of call 9 before ringing (a senior may).
The customer collects the car and pays 722.80 on the afternoon of this call's day.
The customer borrowed a relative's truck for a trip to Knoxville while the car was late.
